Title: May 28, 2026 Boulder City Council Special Meeting and Study Session

Topic1.Title: Consent Agenda: Council Endorsement of Matt Benjamin's CML Executive Board Nomination
Topic1.Summary: Council voted to add item 2A to the consent agenda confirming endorsement of Councilmember Matt Benjamin's nomination to the Colorado Municipal League Executive Board. Benjamin explained CML's role lobbying state legislation and Boulder's two appointed seats. Benjamin recused himself, and the consent agenda passed 8 to 0.

Topic2.Title: Public Hearing: Ordinance 8749 Eminent Domain for Arapahoe Avenue Safety Project
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the Arapahoe Avenue safety improvement project, a $12 million effort with $9.6 million in federal funding and $2.4 million in city funds. Acquiring about 700 square feet from each of 14 properties may require eminent domain authority to keep the schedule and meet the 2030 federal spending deadline, though staff does not expect to use it. One resident spoke against the ordinance during public comment. Council unanimously adopted Ordinance 8749.

Topic3.Title: Matters: Council Direction on Continued Use of Airport Land
Topic3.Summary: Staff asked whether the question of continuing airport operations indefinitely should return as a consent item or a public hearing. Council members favored a public hearing for community input, and a majority voted for that path. Council also directed staff, by a vote of five, to bring back two options and legal research on long-term land encumbrance and FAA grant implications.

Topic4.Title: Study Session: Downtown Development Authority (DDA) Formation Analysis
Topic4.Summary: Staff presented the draft DDA plan of development, a 30-year reinvestment framework covering downtown, University Hill, and connecting corridors. Financing would rely on a 3.67 mill levy replacing existing GID levies, tax increment financing, and parking asset integration. Staff requested direction on feedback to the plan, the financial structure, and drafting ballot measures for November 2026. Council members raised concerns about general fund impacts, parking governance, equity for the Hill, and measuring outcomes, and generally supported moving forward.
